body.x: Verses Inc. (CEO Sean Lee) participated in CES 2025, held from January 7 to 10 (local time) in Las Vegas, as part of the Incheon IFEZ Pavilion. The music tech startup company focuses on creating user-driven music experiences. Unlike traditional music consumption, which revolves solely around listening, Verses offers a next-generation experience in metaverse environments where users can interact with artists, explore music-themed worlds, and control their musical journeys based on personal preferences.

Verses has successfully developed its "Meta Music System" using advanced AI technology. This innovation transforms the act of experiencing music into a playful and creative process, allowing users to engage with music in an unprecedented, tactile way.
At CES 2025, Verses unveiled "Aespa World," an interactive music world created in collaboration with SM Entertainment's girl group Aespa and utilizing Naver's metaverse platform, ZEPETO.

Aespa World allows users to personalize their avatars, meet Aespa members, take photos, dance, and create music videos to share with others. The immersive platform fully integrates Aespa's music and narrative universe, enabling users to move through spaces and directly interact with music, turning passive listening into an active, instrument-like experience.

body.cap: Verses' booth showcasing "Aespa World" at CES 2025. | Photo by AVING News

body.x: The service incorporates tracks such as "Drama," "Supernova," and "Armageddon" into the Aespa World environment, reflecting Aespa's distinctive lore. Verses' prior award-winning technologies, including the Meta Music System and beat-based AI music video generation, play a pivotal role in creating this interactive environment. The company plans to update the platform with new content based on Aespa's discography.
Verses was honored as a CES 2025 Innovation Awards Honoree in the Mobile Devices, Accessories & Apps category for Aespa World, marking the company’s fourth consecutive recognition at CES.

A Verses representative stated, "At this year's CES, we captivated global attendees by introducing our Aespa World service and a groundbreaking multimodal generative music engine that enables the creation of interactive music worlds in the metaverse using just a few prompt words. This innovation drastically reduces the time and cost of producing metaverse music content, opening new opportunities in the music industry."

The company actively seeks global partnerships with investors, buyers, and technology developers. “Through collaborations with clients and corporations in the AI and metaverse sectors, we aim to accelerate business expansion and content development," the representative added.

body.cap: Verses CEO Sean Lee and AVING News reporter Alex Sigrist during an interview at CES 2025. | Photo by AVING News

body.x: AVING News, which has covered CES for 20 consecutive years, continues to support the global ambitions of Korean SMEs and startups through various initiatives.

Before CES 2025, AVING hosted a series of Global Media Meetups featuring aspiring SMEs in Korea. The Meetups introduced Korean SMEs’ technologies, products, and services to media worldwide, expanding connections between the Korean industry and global media. Geekspin, Ubergizmo, Interesting Engineering, and Le Café du Geek participated in these meetups.
During CES 2025, AVING established the AVING Broadcasting Zone at The Venetian Hotel in Las Vegas, interviewing CES Innovation Award 2025 winners.
Following CES 2025, AVING will co-host a review conference with participating companies in Korea, offering them a platform to gain further recognition and enhance their corporate image.
